stem: Meena waters the tulsi plant in her courtyard in Jaipur every morning. One hot afternoon, she asks her teacher why the rain that refills their village pond and helps crops grow does not fall equally everywhere in India. Her teacher draws a chain showing how sunlight, water and moving air work together on Earth. Which chain is correct?

options.text: Rain fills ponds first, and then the Sun heats the rainwater to form clouds that bring more rain.
Sunlight heats water in ponds, rivers and seas; water vapour rises and forms clouds; moving air carries the clouds; rain falls and refills water sources, helping plants and animals live in a place.
Moving air cools the land first, which creates sunlight, and sunlight then makes rain fall from clear skies.
Because most of Earth is covered with water, every place gets the same rainfall, so the same plants and animals can live everywhere.

teacher.key_rationale: B states the correct cause-and-effect chain from the chapter: sunlight heats water, vapour forms clouds, wind moves them, rain refills sources and shapes habitats. A reverses the chain, C invents a false ordering, and D repeats the common overgeneralisation that abundant water means identical habitats everywhere; rainfall differences determine which plants and animals can live in a place.
